title: Jeremiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 42 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 42.

questions.question: Who came near to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 42:1?
options: All the captains of the forces, Johanan the son of Kareah, Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest
Only the captains of the forces
Only Johanan the son of Kareah and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah
The priests and Levites only
questions.correctAnswer: All the captains of the forces, Johanan the son of Kareah, Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:1 states that all the captains of the forces, Johanan the son of Kareah, Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest came near to Jeremiah.

questions.question: What did the people ask Jeremiah to do in Jeremiah 42:2?
options: To pray for them to the LORD their God
To lead them into battle
To build them a temple
To write a new law
questions.correctAnswer: To pray for them to the LORD their God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:2 shows that the people asked Jeremiah to pray for them unto the LORD their God.

questions.question: What reason did the people give for their request in Jeremiah 42:2?
options: They were but a few of many, as Jeremiah's eyes could behold
They wanted to build a new city
They had plenty of food and were prosperous
They wanted to fight the Babylonians
questions.correctAnswer: They were but a few of many, as Jeremiah's eyes could behold
questions.explanation: The verse Jeremiah 42:2 explains that they were left but a few of many, as Jeremiah's eyes did behold them.

questions.question: What did the people want the LORD to show them according to Jeremiah 42:3?
options: The way wherein they might walk and the thing that they might do
The location of hidden treasure
The name of their enemies
How to build a temple
questions.correctAnswer: The way wherein they might walk and the thing that they might do
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:3 states that they asked the LORD to show them the way wherein they might walk, and the thing that they might do.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah say he would do after hearing their request in Jeremiah 42:4?
options: He would pray to the LORD and declare whatever answer the LORD gave
He would refuse to pray for them
He would take them to Egypt
He would write a letter to the king
questions.correctAnswer: He would pray to the LORD and declare whatever answer the LORD gave
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:4 explains that Jeremiah said he would pray to the LORD according to their words and declare whatever the LORD answered, keeping nothing back.

questions.question: What did the people swear to do in Jeremiah 42:5?
options: To do all things according to the LORD's instructions sent through Jeremiah
To build a new city
To flee to Egypt immediately
To ignore the LORD's commands
questions.correctAnswer: To do all things according to the LORD's instructions sent through Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:5 states that the people said the LORD be a true and faithful witness between them if they do not do according to all things that the LORD shall send through Jeremiah.

questions.question: What did the people promise in Jeremiah 42:6?
options: To obey the voice of the LORD whether the message was good or evil
To rebel against the LORD
To return to Egypt immediately
To fight against Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: To obey the voice of the LORD whether the message was good or evil
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:6 says they would obey whether the word was good or evil, so that it might be well with them when they obeyed the voice of the LORD.

questions.question: How many days passed before the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah according to Jeremiah 42:7?
options: Ten days
One day
Seven days
Thirty days
questions.correctAnswer: Ten days
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:7 states that after ten days, the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah.

questions.question: Who did Jeremiah call after receiving the word of the LORD in Jeremiah 42:8?
options: Johanan the son of Kareah, all the captains of the forces, and all the people from the least to the greatest
Only the priests
Only the captains of the forces
The king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Johanan the son of Kareah, all the captains of the forces, and all the people from the least to the greatest
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:8 describes that Jeremiah called Johanan the son of Kareah, all the captains with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah promised to keep some of the LORD's answers secret from the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:4 clearly states he would declare all that the LORD answered and keep nothing back from them.

questions.question: True or False: The people said they would obey the LORD only if the message was good.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:6 shows they promised to obey whether the message was good or evil.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 42:1, Johanan was the son of Kareah.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:1 names Johanan as the son of Kareah.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's word came to Jeremiah immediately after the people requested prayer.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:7 specifies that the LORD's word came after ten days, not immediately.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 42, which action comes first?
options: The people ask Jeremiah to pray for them
Jeremiah receives the word of the LORD
Jeremiah calls Johanan and all the captains
The people swear to obey the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The people ask Jeremiah to pray for them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:2 shows the people first asked Jeremiah to pray for them, before the LORD's word came (verse 7) and before Jeremiah called the captains (verse 8). The swearing to obey is in verse 5, after the initial request.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 42:3, what did the people want the LORD to show them?
options: The way to walk and what to do
The location of their enemies
The future of the kingdom
How to build an altar
questions.correctAnswer: The way to walk and what to do
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:3 states they wanted the LORD to show them the way in which they might walk, and the thing they might do.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 42 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 42:9, who did the people send Jeremiah to present their supplication before?
options: The LORD, the God of Israel
The king of Babylon
The priests in Jerusalem
The people of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD, the God of Israel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:9 states that Jeremiah was sent to present their supplication before the LORD, the God of Israel, showing their reliance on God for guidance.

questions.question: What promise does God give if the people continue to dwell in the land, according to Jeremiah 42:10?
options: God will build and plant them, not pull them down or pluck them up
God will send them to Egypt for protection
God will cause famine to teach them humility
God will remove them from the land permanently
questions.correctAnswer: God will build and plant them, not pull them down or pluck them up
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:10 promises that if they abide in the land, God will build and plant them and not pull them down or uproot them, indicating restoration and blessing.

questions.question: What reason does God give in Jeremiah 42:10 for His change of heart regarding the evil done to the people?
options: Because He repents of the evil He has done
Because the king of Babylon pleaded for mercy
Because the people prepared sacrifices
Because the famine ended
questions.correctAnswer: Because He repents of the evil He has done
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:10 explicitly states that God repents of the evil He has done unto them, showing His mercy and willingness to restore.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 42:11, what should the people not fear, and why?
options: The king of Babylon, because God is with them to save and deliver
The famine, because they will be fed miraculously
The priests, because they will intercede for them
The neighboring nations, because they will flee
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Babylon, because God is with them to save and deliver
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:11 instructs the people not to fear the king of Babylon because the LORD is with them to save and deliver them from his hand.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 42:12 say God will do to help the people return to their own land?
options: Show mercies to them so that Babylon will have mercy upon them
Send a prophet to lead them back
Cause the king of Babylon to be defeated
Remove the famine completely
questions.correctAnswer: Show mercies to them so that Babylon will have mercy upon them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:12 explains that God will show mercies to them, which will cause the king of Babylon to have mercy and allow their return to their land.

questions.question: What consequence does Jeremiah 42:16 describe if the people go into Egypt to sojourn?
options: The sword and famine they feared will overtake them in Egypt, and they shall die there
They will find peace and safety in Egypt
They will become rulers in Egypt
They will be protected from all evil
questions.correctAnswer: The sword and famine they feared will overtake them in Egypt, and they shall die there
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:16 warns that if they go into Egypt, the very dangers they feared—the sword and famine—will catch up with them and cause death there.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 42:13-14 reflect the people's attitude toward God's command to stay in the land?
options: They refuse to dwell in the land and plan to go to Egypt for safety
They eagerly obey and choose to remain in the land
They want to go to Babylon for protection
They intend to return to Jerusalem immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They refuse to dwell in the land and plan to go to Egypt for safety
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 14 show their decision to disobey God by refusing to stay and instead going to Egypt, seeking peace from war and famine.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 42:15 say will happen if the people set their faces to enter Egypt to sojourn?
options: They will face calamity by sword, famine, and pestilence
They will find refuge and safety
They will prosper and multiply
They will be welcomed by the Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: They will face calamity by sword, famine, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Verse 15 warns that setting their faces to enter Egypt will result in death by sword, famine, and pestilence, showing God's judgment upon disobedience.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 42:18, what will be the spiritual and social consequences if the people enter Egypt?
options: They will become an execration, astonishment, curse, and reproach, and will never see the land again
They will be honored and praised by other nations
They will establish a new community in Egypt
They will receive blessings from God
questions.correctAnswer: They will become an execration, astonishment, curse, and reproach, and will never see the land again
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:18 states that entering Egypt will cause them to be cursed and reproached, becoming a disgrace and never returning to their land.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 42:19 describe God's admonition to the remnant of Judah?
options: God commands them not to go into Egypt and assures that He has warned them
God encourages them to seek refuge in Egypt
God tells them to prepare for war
God promises to send a deliverer from Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: God commands them not to go into Egypt and assures that He has warned them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:19 clearly instructs the remnant not to enter Egypt and reminds them that God has given them this warning.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 42:20 accuse the people of when they sent Jeremiah to pray for them?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 accuses the people of dissembling in their hearts, meaning they were insincere when asking Jeremiah to pray and promising obedience.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 42:22, what will be the fate of those who go to sojourn in the place they desire?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:22 confirms that those who choose to go where they desire will die by sword, famine, and pestilence, emphasizing the consequences of disobedience.

questions.question: Does Jeremiah 42:21 say the people obeyed the voice of the LORD after Jeremiah declared His word?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explicitly states that the people did not obey the voice of the LORD nor the message Jeremiah delivered, showing their rebellion.

questions.question: What Christian virtue can be learned from Jeremiah 42:10-12 about trusting God during difficult times?
options: Faith and obedience lead to restoration and mercy
Self-reliance is better than trusting God
Avoiding difficulties at all costs is wise
Ignoring God's commands is acceptable if fearful
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and obedience lead to restoration and mercy
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 teach that trusting and obeying God even in hardship brings His mercy and restoration, highlighting the importance of faithfulness and trust.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 42:16-17, what practical lesson about obedience and consequences can Christians apply?
options: Disobedience leads to inevitable hardship and judgment
Disobedience guarantees immediate blessings
God ignores human choices in difficult times
Avoiding God's will brings peace and safety
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to inevitable hardship and judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 warn that choosing to disobey God’s instruction results in calamity, teaching that obedience is essential to avoid judgment.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 42.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 42:17, what will happen to all the men who set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there?
options: They shall prosper and multiply
They shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence
They shall be taken captive but later freed
They shall find peace and safety
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:17 explicitly states that those who choose to go into Egypt will die by sword, famine, and pestilence without escape.

questions.question: Jeremiah 42:18 describes God's fury as being poured out upon the people when they enter Egypt. Which of the following best describes the consequences mentioned?
options: They will become kings and rulers
They will be an execration, astonishment, curse, and reproach
They will prosper greatly in Egypt
They will build a strong alliance with Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They will be an execration, astonishment, curse, and reproach
questions.explanation: The verse explains that God's fury will cause them to become a curse and reproach, never seeing their land again.

questions.question: What command does the LORD give the remnant of Judah in Jeremiah 42:19?
options: Go into Egypt for safety
Fight against Babylon
Do not go into Egypt
Build houses in the land of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Do not go into Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:19 clearly admonishes the remnant not to go into Egypt, warning them against disobedience.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 42:20, what attitude did the people display when they sent Jeremiah to pray for them?
options: Sincerity and faithfulness
Dissembling in their hearts
Complete trust in God
Joy and obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Dissembling in their hearts
questions.explanation: The verse states they dissembled, meaning they pretended or were deceitful in their hearts despite their words.

questions.question: What was the people's response after Jeremiah declared the LORD's message to them in Jeremiah 42:21?
options: They obeyed the LORD immediately
They rejected the voice of the LORD
They asked for further confirmation
They rejoiced and gave thanks
questions.correctAnswer: They rejected the voice of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:21 says they did not obey the voice of the LORD nor anything for which Jeremiah was sent.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 42:22, what will be the fate of those who go into Egypt?
options: They will live long and prosper
They will die by sword, famine, and pestilence
They will be taken as slaves
They will return safely to Judah
questions.correctAnswer: They will die by sword, famine, and pestilence
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly warns that those going to Egypt will die by these means, emphasizing the certainty of judgment.

questions.question: What promise does God make to the people if they choose to abide in the land, as stated in Jeremiah 42:10?
options: He will build and plant them, not pull them down or pluck them up
He will give them riches and gold
He will make them rulers over other nations
He will send angels to fight for them
questions.correctAnswer: He will build and plant them, not pull them down or pluck them up
questions.explanation: God promises restoration and stability if they stay in their land, showing repentance for past evil.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 42:11, why should the people not fear the king of Babylon?
options: Because Babylon will soon be destroyed
Because God is with them to save and deliver
Because they have superior armies
Because Babylon has no interest in their land
questions.correctAnswer: Because God is with them to save and deliver
questions.explanation: The LORD assures them of His presence and protection against Babylon’s king.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word study related question fits Jeremiah 42:13-14 about going into Egypt?
options: What does the Hebrew word for 'famine' indicate about the nature of the threat?
What is the meaning of the Hebrew word for 'Egypt' used here?
What does the Hebrew term translated as 'sojourn' imply about their stay in Egypt?
What does the Hebrew word for 'fear' signify in this context?
questions.correctAnswer: What does the Hebrew term translated as 'sojourn' imply about their stay in Egypt?
questions.explanation: The term 'sojourn' (גר, 'ger') in Hebrew implies a temporary stay, highlighting their intent to dwell without permanent settlement, which is significant in the warning.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of disobedience and its consequences found in Jeremiah 42:20-22?
options: Deuteronomy 28:15-68
Psalm 23
Genesis 1:1-5
Revelation 21:1-7
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 28:15-68
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28 details blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience, paralleling Jeremiah’s warnings about the fate of those who disobey God.

questions.question: Jeremiah 42:16-17 foreshadow which later historical event in Israel's history?
options: The Babylonian exile and destruction of Jerusalem
The conquest of Canaan under Joshua
The Exodus from Egypt
The rebuilding of the temple under Ezra
questions.correctAnswer: The Babylonian exile and destruction of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The warnings about death by sword, famine, and pestilence foreshadow the catastrophic exile and destruction Jerusalem faced under Babylon.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Jeremiah 42:18 when describing the people as 'an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach'?
options: Chiasmus
Parallelism
Allegory
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The verse uses parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, repeating similar ideas in a structured way to emphasize the severity of judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 42:7-9 demonstrate the theme of prophetic mediation?
options: Jeremiah ignores the people's request
Jeremiah prays and then faithfully delivers God's word to the people
Jeremiah changes the message to please the people
Jeremiah refuses to speak on God's behalf
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah prays and then faithfully delivers God's word to the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah acts as a mediator by praying to God for guidance and then openly declaring God's response to the people.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 42:6 reveal about the people's commitment to God's word through Jeremiah?
options: They will obey only if it is convenient
They promise to obey whether the message is good or evil
They refuse to listen to any prophecy
They ask for a delayed response
questions.correctAnswer: They promise to obey whether the message is good or evil
questions.explanation: The people swear to obey all that the LORD commands, showing their pledge to accept God's word fully.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 42:20-21 indicates that the people were fully honest and sincere when they sent Jeremiah to pray for them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:20 explicitly states the people dissembled in their hearts, showing insincerity despite their spoken words.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 42 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 42 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What do the captains of the forces request from Jeremiah?
options: To pray for them
To lead them into battle
To appoint a new king
To offer sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: To pray for them
questions.explanation: The captains requested Jeremiah to pray for them before the LORD, expressing their supplication in Jeremiah 42:2.

questions.question: What promise does the LORD make if the people abide in the land?
options: He will destroy their enemies
He will build them up and plant them
He will give them riches
He will send them prophets
questions.correctAnswer: He will build them up and plant them
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 42:10, the LORD promises that if they stay in the land, He will build them and not pull them down, demonstrating His desire for restoration.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah, what should the people not fear?
options: The king of Babylon
The famine
The pestilence
Their own hearts
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:11 tells the people not to be afraid of the king of Babylon, as the LORD assures them of His presence and deliverance.

questions.question: What will happen if the remnant of Judah goes to Egypt?
options: They will prosper
They will escape the sword
They shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence
They will be blessed by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:17 warns that those who choose to go into Egypt will face death by the sword, famine, and pestilence.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'execration, astonishment, curse, and reproach' refer to?
options: The promises of God
The fate of those who enter Egypt
The blessings of obedience
The words of Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: The fate of those who enter Egypt
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 42:18, the LORD describes the severe consequences and disgrace that will befall those who enter Egypt.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah say about the people's intentions in their hearts?
options: They truly want to follow God
They are deceitful
They are courageous
They are confused
questions.correctAnswer: They are deceitful
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:20 reveals that the people dissembled in their hearts when they sought the LORD's guidance, indicating their insincerity.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah declare about the people's response to God's voice?
options: They have obeyed
They will obey in the future
They did not obey
They were confused about it
questions.correctAnswer: They did not obey
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 42:21, Jeremiah states that the people have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, highlighting their disobedience.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 10 and 11 convey about God's relationship with His people?
options: God desires to punish His people
God promises to be with His people and protect them
God is indifferent to their fate
God encourages them to flee
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to be with His people and protect them
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 emphasize God's commitment to build and protect His people if they remain in the land, assuring them of His presence.

questions.question: What does the term 'remnant' signify in this chapter?
options: A group of wealthy people
The faithful few left after judgment
A rebellious faction
A new generation
questions.correctAnswer: The faithful few left after judgment
questions.explanation: The use of 'remnant' in Jeremiah 42 refers to the small group of Judah that remains faithful amidst widespread disobedience and judgment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'ten days' mentioned in Jeremiah 42:7?
options: It indicates a period of waiting for God's response
It symbolizes a full cycle of judgment
It represents a time for celebration
It has no significance
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates a period of waiting for God's response
questions.explanation: The ten days in Jeremiah 42:7 signifies a waiting period for the people to receive God's word through Jeremiah, illustrating their dependence on divine guidance.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by the promise of mercy in Jeremiah 42:12?
options: Justice
Grace
Holiness
Omniscience
questions.correctAnswer: Grace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:12 emphasizes God's grace in promising to show mercy to His people, allowing for their return to the land despite their disobedience.

questions.question: What does the phrasing 'I will keep nothing back from you' indicate about Jeremiah's role?
options: He is a mediator
He is a false prophet
He is disobedient
He is indifferent
questions.correctAnswer: He is a mediator
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's commitment in Jeremiah 42:4 to declare all that God answers signifies his role as a faithful mediator between God and the people.

questions.question: What combined insight do verses 5-6 and verse 19 convey about obedience?
options: Obedience leads to blessings
Obedience is unnecessary
Disobedience is acceptable
Obedience is only for leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience leads to blessings
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 emphasize the people's commitment to obey, and verse 19 warns of the consequences of failing to obey, illustrating that obedience is essential for well-being.

questions.question: What does the LORD's command not to go to Egypt reveal about His sovereignty?
options: He is powerless against Babylon
He desires to protect His people
He is indifferent to their choices
He cannot control their actions
questions.correctAnswer: He desires to protect His people
questions.explanation: The LORD's command in Jeremiah 42:19 demonstrates His sovereignty in guiding His people away from danger and towards His protective will.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care about the decisions of His people. What does Jeremiah 42:19-22 actually teach?
options: God is indifferent to their fate
God actively guides and warns His people
God is only concerned with the leaders
God has abandoned His people
questions.correctAnswer: God actively guides and warns His people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:19-22 illustrates God's active involvement in the decisions of His people, as He warns them against going to Egypt and outlines the consequences of disobedience.
